localChanges: New Game → Rules → Enhanced rules for a Civilization II game has two new rules, both off to start with, as Civilization games already do. With the first, each civilization moves through four ages (the Ancient Age, the Renaissance, the Industrial Age and the Modern Age) as it learns its first advance from a later era, and you are told when yours does (#1076). With the second, research costs less in the early ages and more in the later ones, judged by your own age, so a whole game costs about as much as it does today (#1077).

log: `civ2-enhanced:ages`: each civilization moves through Civilization II's four epochs as ages (Ancient, Renaissance, Industrial, Modern), by the latest epoch among the advances it knows, with `base-science-age` as `civ1-enhanced`'s are. An advance's epoch is RULES.TXT's @CIVILIZE column, which the original uses only for its picture; no advance's epoch is earlier than one it needs. It is told once per age, by any way of gaining an advance, and not for the advances a civilization starts with or inherits in a civil war, as `civ1-enhanced`'s.

`civ2-enhanced:research-cost-by-age`: the research cost times the player's own age's multiplier, 0.5, 0.66, 0.88 and 1.17, with either research cost, through `civ2-science`'s new `RateMultiplier` (Civilization II has no factor of its own, so the set supersedes nothing). The slide starts at half, as Civilization's does, and rises by 1.328 an age, chosen so that learning every advance along the steady path, each at its player's age before it, costs 0.998 times what it does today by Civilization II's cost (0.996 by the fixed costs); along the computer players' own choices, about 1.04 times. The Modern carries about three fifths of the cost, so Civilization's slide to 3 would make research about 2.3 times as dear. A person's floor stays with Civilization II's own cost. There is no catch-up by the calendar to move: Civilization II's ahead-of-the-turn term already depends on the player's own advances. The README's note on civ2-score's pollution term now says it discounts all the pollution near computer players' cities, not half.

Civilization II's cost has no factor of its own to replace, as Civilization's doubling from AD is, so this adds a `RateMultiplier` rule and registers none: with none in force the cost is Civilization II's own, unchanged and unrounded. A rule set that adds one (civ2-enhanced's research cost by age) has the cost multiplied and rounded to a whole bulb before it stops at 32000 (`lib/cost`'s `multipliedCost`), so the person's floor stays inside the ratio as today. The cost rule asks the game's rules when given them, as `registerRules` does; left out, as before.
